extracted.intended_audience: researchers, systematic reviewers, meta-analysts, journal editors, and guideline developers in health research
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and reporting criteria for planning, conducting, and reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses (and related primary trials and diagnostic/observational studies) in health care. Focuses on named guideline documents, ethical and methodological expectations, and recommended practices for transparency and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICMJE criteria for authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: ICMJE criteria for authorship read and met: AL DGA JT CM PCG JPAI MC PJD JK DM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the authorship standard for the manuscript; statement indicates all named authors met the ICMJE authorship criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized controlled trials registration/application checklist (CIHR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomized controlled trials registration/application checklist (12/2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registry/registration checklist referenced as a requirement for trial registration and application; URL and access date provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: QUOROM statement (Quality of Reporting of Meta-analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improving the quality of reports of meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials: The QUOROM statement. Quality of Reporting of Meta-analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named as a reporting standard for meta-analyses of RCTs; used historically as a checklist to improve completeness and transparency of meta-analysis reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses: The PRISMA Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as the reporting checklist for systematic reviews and meta-analyses; reference to PRISMA Group and the PRISMA statement paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT statement (revised)
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised CONSORT statement for reporting randomized trials: Explanation and elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CONSORT recommended for reporting randomized controlled trials, including guidance for abstracts and full reports; cited evidence about CONSORT checklist improving quality of reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT for abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT for reporting randomized trials in journal and conference abstracts: Explanation and elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific recommendation to follow CONSORT guidance when preparing abstracts of randomized trials to improve clarity and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD statement
rubrics_metrics.description: For reporting studies of diagnostic accuracy: The STARD statement — Explanation and elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended checklist for complete reporting of diagnostic accuracy studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE): Explanation and elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reporting standard for observational epidemiologic studies to ensure clarity and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: EQUATOR network (reporting guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: EQUATOR: Reporting guidelines for health research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EQUATOR presented as the coordinating network/resource for reporting guideline development and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of Helsinki (ethical principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: World Medical Association Declaration of Helsinki: Ethical principles for medical research involving human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as the ethical standard for human-subject research that should inform trial conduct and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin and end trial reports with up-to-date systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of clinical trials should begin and end with up-to-date systematic reviews of other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation that trial reports place the trial in context by referencing current systematic reviews at both the start and end of reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish protocols for systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing protocols of systematic reviews: Comparing what was done to what was planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to publish review protocols to allow comparison between planned methods and completed review, reducing selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing risk of bias in included studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter 8: Assessing risk of bias in included studies (Cochrane Handbook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviews should assess risk of bias of included studies using established methods (per Cochrane Handbook guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE: rating quality and strength of recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: GRADE: An emerging consensus on rating quality of evidence and strength of recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use GRADE to rate overall quality of evidence and to frame strength of recommendations based on review findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive, reproducible search strategies and expert searcher involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimal search strategies for retrieving systematic reviews — reporting of the role of expert searcher in Cochrane reviews; benchmarking and evaluation of search/selection methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviews should use validated, comprehensive search strategies, report methods in detail, and involve trained information specialists where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of publication and reporting biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical evidence for selective reporting of outcomes in randomized trials; systematic reviews of publication/reporting bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should assess and address publication bias and selective outcome reporting (e.g., compare protocols to publications, use methods to detect bias).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include non-English and 'grey' literature considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies on language bias and grey literature in meta-analyses of randomized trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the impact of language restrictions and inclusion of grey literature on review results; evaluate for language and location biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and manage duplicate/overlapping publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Different patterns of duplicate publication and impact of covert duplicate publication on meta-analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviews should identify and handle duplicate publications to avoid inflating evidence and biasing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and report methodological quality of primary studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of methodological quality of primary studies by systematic reviews; tools for assessing quality and susceptibility to bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate established tools/checklists to evaluate study quality and report those assessments transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report adverse events and harms in systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of adverse events in systematic reviews can be improved: survey results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviews should systematically collect, analyse, and transparently report adverse events and harms data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate statistical methods and heterogeneity handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and empirical studies on fixed vs random effects models, meta-regression, heterogeneity, and summary statistic selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and justify appropriate meta-analytic models (fixed/random), conduct and report heterogeneity assessments, and use appropriate summary statistics and sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing variance and data imputation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Variance imputation for overviews and lack of standardization in methods for handling missing variance data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviewers should use and report appropriate methods for dealing with missing variance data and justify imputation approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about funding, conflicts, and sponsorship effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence on pharmaceutical industry sponsorship and research outcome and quality; financial ties and concordance between results and conclusions in meta-analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources and conflicts of interest and consider potential influence of sponsorship on study conduct, reporting, and conclusions.
